title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Sophie Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook consolidates Redwood's Applied ML evaluation practices: the eval harness, standardized prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and regression triage procedures. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and platform owners responsible for model evaluation, deployment readiness, and ongoing quality monitoring.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-production for new model variants while maintaining output quality and cost targets.
- Provide a single operational flow for onboarding, validating, and triaging model regressions.
- Make quantization decisions predictable and auditable by coupling profiles with eval results.
- Ensure reproducible, automated evaluations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope & Audience:
- Scope: text-generation and chat-capable models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder variants), embedding models where relevant.
- Audience: Applied ML, Platform, SRE, and Product teams.

Principles:
1) Evaluation-first: Every model change that affects inference code, weights, or quantization must pass the eval harness before rollouts.
2) Representative prompts: Use per-product prompt sets that mirror real traffic distribution and edge case coverage.
3) Metric-driven decisions: Primary metrics (ROUGE/EM/Exact Match for targeted tasks, embedding cosine stability, perplexity for general quality) plus business-specific metrics (latency, token cost, hallucination rate).
4) Fast feedback loops: Automated daily regression checks and on-demand pre-rollout suites.
5) Traceability: All eval runs must link to model version, quantization profile, and config used.

Components & Responsibilities:
- Eval Harness (owner: applied-ml):
  - Central test runner that executes prompt sets, computes metrics, and stores results in the eval database.
  - Must support: deterministic seeding, configurable temperature/top_p, batching/streaming modes, and model variant definitions (fp16, int8, q4_0, q3_k, etc.).
  - Integrations: CI (pre-merge), Model Registry (metadata), Observability (push metrics), and Canary pipelines.

- Prompt Sets & Benchmarks (owner: applied-ml + product SMEs):
  - Each product has three canonical prompt sets: production-sample, edge-cases, adversarial/guardrails.
  - Benchmarks include: customer-SLO-critical tasks, privacy-sensitive examples, and token-efficiency workloads.
  - Maintain dataset manifest with metadata: source, input distribution weight, acceptance thresholds, and example tags.

- Model Onboarding Guide (owner: applied-ml):
  - Checklist (must complete before canary):
    1) Register model: model-id, git-hash, training-data-tag, base-architecture, expected FLOPS.
    2) Baseline eval: run full eval-suite vs. current production on production-sample and edge sets.
    3) Latency/cost profiling: collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, and per-token cost estimate under target batching.
    4) Quantization compatibility test: run quick pass with desired quantization profile.
    5) Safety & privacy scan: run guardrail prompts and PII detectors.
    6) Review & sign-off: applied-ml reviewer and product owner sign-off recorded in model registry.

- Quality Guardrails (owner: applied-ml + security):
  - Guardrail checklist includes: harmful content detection, policy violations, PII leakage, hallucination heuristics, and format regressions for structured outputs.
  - Thresholds: define per-product maximum allowed violation rate (e.g., <=0.5% high-severity, <=2% medium-severity).
  - Automated mitigation: failing models are blocked from canary rollout; enable automatic fallback to production model for affected routes.

- Quantization Profiles (owner: applied-ml + eng-serving-runtime):
  - Profiles are named and versioned (e.g., q_profile_v2-int8-lowram). Each profile includes: target bits, per-layer exceptions, calibration seed, and recommended kernel set.
  - Profile decision matrix:
    - When to apply: latency-critical routes with tolerable accuracy delta <= 2% (task-specific).
    - When to avoid: sensitive NLP tasks (legal, clinical) or structured-output tasks with strict formatting constraints.
  - Calibration & validation: run calibration on held-out corpus, then full eval-suite comparing fp16 baseline to quantized variant. Store diff metrics and confidence intervals.

- Regression Triage Playbook (owner: applied-ml + customer-success):
  - Triggering events: daily regression alerts, post-deploy regressions, customer-reported quality drops.
  - Triage steps (ordered):
    1) Ingest: collect failing examples, model version(s), quantization profile, and request traces.
    2) Classify: determine whether failure is data shift, model drift, quantization-induced, infra (latency/timeouts), or prompt-format change.
    3) Reproduce: re-run eval-harness with the failing examples against candidate model variants.
    4) Mitigate: if quantization is suspected, quickly rerun with fp16/previous quant profile and consider rollback. If infra, escalate to SRE.
    5) Root cause: deeper analysis (attention maps, token-level log-likelihoods, prompt sensitivity).
    6) Resolution & postmortem: document findings, corrective actions, monitoring changes, and lessons learned.

Automated Workflows & CI Integration:
- Pre-merge hooks: lightweight eval on representative mini-set (10-50 examples) with unit thresholds.
- Pre-release pipeline: full eval-suite including latency/cost profile; must pass quality gates to trigger canary.
- Canary builds: smoke tests, subset of production traffic, continuous regression monitoring for 48-72 hours.
- Scheduled regression scans: nightlies that re-run critical benchmarks against production model to detect silent regressions.

Metrics & Dashboards:
- Core metrics to publish per-model and per-quantization-profile: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, token-cost-estimate, task-specific accuracy (EM/F1/ROUGE), hallucination-rate, guardrail-violation-rate.
- Alert rules: trigger on +5% drop vs baseline for task accuracy or +2x increase in guardrail violations.
- Dashboards: per-product and global overviews with links to failing prompt examples and eval run artifacts.

Templates & Example Commands:
- Eval harness run (example):
  - CLI: eval-harness run --model-id mymodel:v2 --profile q_profile_v2-int8 --prompt-set product-x --seed 42 --out results/mymodel_v2_qprofile.json
- Quick reproduction for a failing example: re-run single-example evaluation with deterministic seeding and logs enabled.

Ownership & SLAs:
- Applied-ML: maintain prompt sets, eval harness, and quantization profiles (SLA: respond to triage requests <= 48 hours).
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: ensure quantized kernels are supported and provide perf baselines (SLA: 72-hour turnaround on kernel issues).
- Customer Success: coordinate with customers during regressions and own customer-facing communications.

Escalation Paths:
1) Severity P0 (customer outage or severe production-quality regression): page oncall SRE and applied-ml lead immediately.
2) Severity P1 (degraded quality affecting key customers): notify product and customer success; prepare rollback plan.
3) Lower severities handled via normal triage with applied-ml owner.

Appendix A — Minimal Model Onboarding Checklist (table format represented as bullet list for portability):
- Model metadata registered (model-id, git-hash, training-data-tag)
- Baseline eval passed (production-sample)
- Edge-case evals reviewed
- Latency & cost profile attached
- Quantization profile validated (or explicitly opted-out)
- Guardrail checks passed
- Product & applied-ml sign-off recorded

Appendix B — Common Regression Signatures & Likely Causes:
- Systematic token truncation + format breaks -> batching/kernel bug or tokenizer change.
- Random answer collapse to short replies -> context window misconfiguration or KV-cache bug.
- Increased hallucinations on a topic -> training data drift or prompt mismatch.
- Single-example failures only on quantized variant -> quantization precision loss or layer-exception missing.

Related Artifacts & Links:
- Eval harness codebase: internal repo link (add to model registry entry).
- Prompt set manifests: stored in dataset service with versioning.
- Quantization profiles: stored in profiles repo with changelog.

Maintenance & Review Cycle:
- Prompt sets: review quarterly, or on major product feature changes.
- Quantization profiles: review with every major runtime release and after any kernel changes.
- Eval harness: CI-driven tests run nightly; full audits annually.

Contact & Support:
- Primary contact: applied-ml@redwood-inference.internal
- Oncall (triage): see eng-sre oncall roster

This playbook is a living document. Changes to the eval harness, prompt sets, quantization profiles, or triage flow should be recorded here with a short summary and the author name.
